company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by 145 basis points of tariff refund tailwind and 105 basis points of non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps disappointed at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, though management noted positive comp linearity in the quarter. The stock is rallying as the linearity commentary provides reassurance despite the mixed quality of the beat.

MillerKnoll reported solid fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, and importantly would have beaten even excluding tariff refunds — ex-refunds EPS was 42 cents, still ahead of consensus. Guidance is mixed with fiscal 2027 sales range trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged. The quality of the earnings beat is notable and the stock is an outperformer on the session.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street at 87 cents, with gross margin weakness of 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% more than offsetting slightly better-than-expected revenue of $2.311 billion. Management cited a difficult macro landscape. The miss on margins and the cautious macro tone are the key negatives.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's keynote at Meta Connect Wednesday night, and Shopify has agreed to allow Muse to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform — a meaningful distribution win. Amazon has blocked Muse from its platform, which is a notable competitive friction point. Investor expectations are building bullishly into the Wednesday event.

Shopify will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases directly on its e-commerce platform, positioning Shopify as a key partner in the emerging agentic commerce ecosystem. This contrasts with Amazon's decision to block Muse, potentially giving Shopify a differentiated edge in AI-driven shopping. The partnership is a modest positive catalyst for the stock.

Quest Diagnostics shares were hit Tuesday after CMS released new Medicare payment rates for lab services that represented a larger reduction than the market had anticipated. The rate cuts are sector-wide and weigh on near-term earnings visibility. This is a regulatory-driven headwind with no immediate offset.

Lab Corp shares dropped alongside Quest Diagnostics after CMS announced Medicare lab service rate cuts that were larger than expected. The move is a direct hit to reimbursement rates and pressures the earnings outlook for both major lab testing companies. The stock is among the notable underperformers on the session.

Alibaba unveiled what it called China's most powerful AI chip and hinted at plans to train a model with up to 10 trillion parameters, while management discussed operating more than 20 gigawatts of data center capacity by 2032. The announcements position Alibaba as a serious competitor in the global AI infrastructure race. This is a significant escalation in China's AI ambitions and a positive catalyst for the stock.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. The deal expands Cognex's capabilities in robotic vision at a time when Physical AI demand is accelerating. The strategic fit is strong but the price tag is meaningful.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, including 22% weight loss in the study. This is a meaningful clinical milestone in the highly competitive GLP-1 obesity drug space. The results are a bullish catalyst and reinforce Viking's positioning as a credible competitor to Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly.

tts_summary:
Here is your midday market update for Tuesday, September 22nd.

Markets are mostly spinning their wheels. The S&P 500 is flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, but the Dow is lagging, down 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is just under a hundred dollars a barrel, off fractionally, as there are some early signs of diplomatic progress around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz — Iran reportedly offered to reopen Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure, and Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline appears to be coming back online at least partially. Gold, silver, and bitcoin are all modestly lower. There is no Fed catalyst driving things today — this is a geopolitics and earnings day.

On the earnings front: AutoZone beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share at fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street's fifty-four dollars and three cents, but the beat was low quality — tariff refunds and a non-cash LIFO benefit juiced gross margins by a combined two hundred fifty basis points, and domestic comps disappointed at plus one point six percent versus the Street's plus three point one percent. Management did say comp linearity was positive through the quarter, which is why the stock is rallying.

MillerKnoll was a cleaner beat — fifty-three cents versus the Street at thirty-six cents, and even stripping out tariff refund tailwinds, adjusted earnings per share was forty-two cents, still comfortably ahead of consensus. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly but EPS outlook held. Stock is an outperformer.

THOR Industries missed — seventy-eight cents versus the Street at eighty-seven cents — with gross margins falling two hundred thirty basis points year-over-year. Management cited a tough macro backdrop.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive phase results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug, showing twenty-two percent weight loss. That's a meaningful clinical win in one of the most competitive drug categories on the planet.

In AI, Meta is the story heading into Wednesday night's Connect keynote. The Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads, and Shopify just agreed to let Muse complete purchases directly on its platform — a real distribution win. OpenAI is reportedly working on a competing product. Alibaba unveiled what it called China's most powerful AI chip and hinted at a model with up to ten trillion parameters. The AI catalyst calendar over the next ten days — Meta Connect Wednesday, OpenAI DevDay on the twenty-ninth, Micron earnings on the thirtieth — is as dense as it gets.

On the negative side: Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp both got hit after CMS released Medicare lab service rate cuts that were larger than anticipated. Financials are broadly weak — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all in the red. And Texas Governor Abbott halted new data center permitting, following his earlier move to block grid connections, which is a fresh headwind for AI infrastructure sentiment.

Directionally, the market lacks conviction today but the AI trade has clear near-term catalysts to run into. Watch the Meta keynote Wednesday night — that is the next major inflection point.
